chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

A neighbour of mine married a woman. So when he intended to copulate with her, she kicked him with her leg and ruptured his testicle, so it became swollen. So after that he copulated with her and a child was born to him. So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that, and about a man whose navel was struck and ruptured. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Regarding all ruptures is a third of the wergild.'
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for rupturing the testicles or navel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific compensation (diyah) for injuries to the testicles and navel, establishing a one-third wergild rate. It highlights the juristic reasoning that despite the potential for sterility, the injury does not constitute total loss of function, as evidenced by the man's continued fertility. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for categorizing partial functional impairments versus fatal wounds.
